svg.title: herdr-dia, as it would look in Dia
svg.desc: Four drawings. One: the Morning Brief listing pull requests waiting on the reader, each with a Review with an agent button. Two: a pull request tab with the chat beside the page, showing a running agent session and the partial review it has written so far. Three: the same tab with the finished review, a recommendation to request changes, two findings with file and line, and Post as comment and Apply the fixes buttons above a field for replying to the agent. Four: the settings, with the repos root, GitHub identity, coding agent, review default of Plan or Auto, repository and favorite author filters, and a checkbox for unapproved pull requests only.
svg.text: herdr-dia, as it would look in Dia
Four moments in a morning: the brief hands a pull request to an agent, the agent works beside the page, the review comes back with the decision next to it, and the settings decide who and what runs.
Keep the unsaved harvest plan when the tab reloads
Retry a stale moisture reading before skipping the zone
Return 409 instead of 500 on duplicate crate ids
The agent works beside the page
Reading the diff and the existing comments.
The session check is right for the signed-in
path. I am still working through what happens
when the session has lapsed: the basket is
resolved from a value on the request, and I
want to see whether anything re-checks who
owns it before it is returned. Nothing posted yet.
Tell the agent how to proceed…
The review comes back with the decision
An expired session restores a basket by id
Tell the agent how to proceed…
Settings decide who and what runs
Plan — the agent proposes; you decide
Every repository, author and pull request is invented. This is a drawing of how the extension would look built into Dia, not a screenshot; the panel as it runs today is in the report above.
